title: Cabin Window Pane Assembly Change on Withdrawal of the Acrylic Supply

ata.title: Passenger Compartment Windows — Cabin Window Assembly

abstract: Requalification of the cabin window pane assembly on a replacement stretched acrylic, after the original sheet supplier stopped making the grade used for the outer pane and no equivalent was available from the existing source.

sections.reason: The stretched acrylic grade used for the cabin window outer pane was discontinued in 2025 when its only producer closed the casting line. Roughly 220 panes a year are consumed across the fleet through crazing, scratching and impact damage, and the stock held by the pane manufacturer covers about three years. Without a requalified pane the aircraft would be limited by window availability rather than by anything structural, which for a fleet with fifteen years of life left is not acceptable to the operators or to the authority.
sections.description: The outer pane is requalified on a replacement stretched acrylic of similar modulus but different craze resistance, which requires a change to the retaining arrangement rather than to the pane geometry. The upper cleat kit D5620110598197 is replaced by an item with a wider land so that the edge stress at the retainer is reduced, and the lower plate kit D5620113496156 is renewed. The upper fitting D5620116475200 is retained. The outboard doubler IBD743967-79 at the frame interface is replaced by a version with a revised sealing groove, and blind rivets AES808479K3 secure the revised retainer. The sidewall trim panel is cut back locally to clear the wider land, to a cutout profile defined by this change. The window assembly stringer D5620110905714 is unchanged. The passenger compartment window actuator at FIN 471WY, which drives the electronic shade on aircraft that have it, is unaffected. Work is from inside the cabin in zones 253, 265 and 274 with the trim panel removed; no external access is needed. Detail is on drawings D56201126385 and D56200077178.
sections.effects: Estimated mass increase of 0.4 kg per window, and on a full aircraft set of 220 windows that is 88 kg distributed along the cabin with no reportable centre-of-gravity effect. No electrical load change. The new pane is one-way interchangeable: the revised retainer accepts either pane, but the original retainer accepts only the original pane, so an aircraft may run mixed during the transition. Craze inspection thresholds change and the published scratch blend limits are reduced slightly. Structure repair content for the window frame and the illustrated parts content for the window assembly both require update.
sections.embodiment_note: Retrofit through spares as panes are consumed rather than as a campaign, with the revised retainer fitted whenever a window is opened. Provisional estimate is two hours per window. No production cut-in is proposed.
sections.open_points: Pre-analysis must establish whether the reduced blend limits invalidate any published window frame repair, whether a mixed pane standard on one aircraft is acceptable to all authorities, and what the transition means for operators that hold pane stock of the original grade.

type_data.balance_impact: Distributed along the cabin, no reportable CG effect
